messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — p99 latency breach on canary pool (canary-v12). p99 ~ 3.8s, streaming stalls surge. triggered at 3519990000

sanjay: I'm oncall, grabbing dashboards and traces.

alex: noticed the spike right after the canary ramp to 40% traffic. p99 jumps aligned with new tokenizer rollout. streaming sessions showing long stalls.

emily: any reports from customers yet? Support watchers?

maria: Support: two high-urgency tickets from GreenWave and DataFlow. both report stalled streaming sessions and reconnect storms. I've tagged customer-impact.

dave: quick metrics dump:
- qps: 1500 -> 1620
- p50: 90ms -> 120ms
- p95: 210ms -> 700ms
- p99: 1.1s -> 3.8s
- streaming-stalls/sec: 5 -> 78
- kv-cache-miss: 2% -> 23%

sanjay: traces show cache churn and heavy recompute on long prefixes. looks like tokenization changes altered shard keys. also see increased request batching size leading to head-of-line blocking.

ops-bot: runbook: canary-latency (https://redwood.internal/runbooks/canary-latency) recommends rollback or traffic-throttle.

alex: mitigation options:
1) immediately stop canary ramp (freeze) and shift traffic back to v11
2) disable batching for canary pool
3) enable model-variant fallback for streaming

maria: prefer staged rollback: 40% -> 20% -> 0% to avoid thundering change across dedicated pools. but if stalls keep rising, we should full rollback.

sanjay: agree but KV-churn is time sensitive. I'll start traffic-controller action to move 40% -> 10% now.

sanjay: /deploy traffic-shift --service api-canary --from canary-v12 --to canary-v11 --percent 30

pagerduty-bot: @sanjay acknowledged. Change accepted by traffic-controller.

alex: applying batching override for canary nodes to reduce head-of-line. command:
```
redwoodctl set-config --pool canary --batching.max-window=0ms
```

dave: override applied at 3519990065. batching disabled for canary.

emily: support sent provisional update to GreenWave: "we're rolling back the canary and expect normal streaming within ~10-15 minutes". asked for trace ids; they provided 3.

maria: enabling variant-fallback now. monitor for increased fallback errors.

sanjay: traffic-controller progress: 40% -> 20% -> 5% in 4 minutes. final shift to v11 started at 3519990140.

ops-bot: note: consider rolling restarts of canary pool to clear stale KV entries. scheduling rolling restart to avoid simultaneous evictions.

alex: restart command queued:
```
redwoodctl restart-pool --pool canary --parallel 1 --grace 20s
```

dave: restarts rolling 3519990200 onward.

maria: mid-mitigation snapshot (3519990250):
- p95: 700ms -> 220ms
- p99: 3.8s -> 320ms
- streaming-stalls/sec: 78 -> 9
- kv-cache-miss: 23% -> 4%

emily: GreenWave confirms streaming back; DataFlow reports reconnections but no data loss. Support lowering urgency to medium. Closing one ticket if stable.

sanjay: preliminary root cause: tokenizer-change in canary-v12 altered token boundary heuristics causing different prefixing behavior and higher KV cache key cardinality. combined with aggressive client-side batching it amplified head-of-line stalls. immediate fix: rollback + disable batching. longer term: add tokenizer-stability checks in model onboarding and KV-key diff tests.

alex: action items:
- SRE postmortem doc + timeline (owner: sanjay)
- onboarding test: automated KV-key-diff + tokenization snapshot (owner: emily)
- traffic ramp guard: cap canary ramp to +10% per 15m by default (owner: maria)
- add a canary health gating check on streaming-stall-rate (owner: dave)

sanjay: handing over monitoring to alex for next 30m. I'll draft the incident timeline and start the postmortem skeleton.

alex: ack. monitoring until 3519990600. will reopen paging if p99 > 500ms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated. cause: tokenizer-induced KV churn + batching-induced stalls. remediation: rollback v12, disable batching, rolling restart. Please publish postmortem link in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: Tickets updated: #4521 GreenWave -> awaiting customer confirm; #4522 DataFlow -> in progress; #4523 follow-up automated alert configured.

sanjay: handing off to oncall next shift @maria. paging cleared.
